scope: Independent still/source review only, prior to parent repairs. All 19 contact sheets (218 actual project shot midframes) inspected, plus four full-size frames.

findings.observation: Narration says By lunch, he had created a small family of documents, but the pictured subject is a steaming bowl with A REAL BREAK. The lunch keyword is temporal, not an eating event.
findings.repair: Route this sentence to document-family or version-file imagery.

findings.observation: Ben waits for another task and nothing has yet happened, but picture shows MORE WORK and a new stack.
findings.repair: Show empty incoming tray or paused task queue, with expectant rather than overloaded acting.

findings.observation: Cold lunch returned to fridge is represented as steaming bowl and A REAL BREAK.
findings.repair: Remove steam, show cold bowl/fridge or lowered lunch tray; avoid positive break headline.

findings.observation: Narration says Ben stopped taking his walk, but image shows him happily outside under AFTER WORK.
findings.repair: Show interrupted/crossed-out walking plan or Ben remaining at desk.

findings.observation: Mara was not standing outside the machine is a metaphor about the workplace hierarchy; generic outside/phone scene does not show Mara or that relationship.
findings.repair: Show Mara on a second work belt or in her own overloaded office.

findings.observation: A lunch break marked tentative is shown as an actual steaming meal with A REAL BREAK.
findings.repair: Use calendar lunch block labelled tentative instead of an actual enjoyed meal.

findings.observation: The first test arrived before lunch is shown as A REAL BREAK with bowl, omitting the arriving test/request.
findings.repair: Show incoming request and existing queue; lunch is only a time reference.

findings.observation: Outside STAND pose visibly plants Ben feet on bench seat, making him stand on the bench rather than beside it. Full-size frames confirm the contact.
findings.repair: Place actor on ground beside the bench or author a seated pose.

findings.observation: LET'S TALK heading end touches/merges with Ben hair/top of head in meeting layout.
findings.repair: Reserve heading band; move actor right or down, or change title width/placement.

findings.observation: Small experiment sequence mostly repeats the same complete pipeline for sample sorting, extraction, report, and human check; key causal steps do not have distinguishable pictured states in the midframes.
findings.repair: Use story-specific source, extraction, draft and human-review states; inspect continuous motion before claiming progression.

findings.observation: Totals checked, attachments checked, permission to feel happy, waiting, quiet factory and quiet head reuse stopwatch + same upright Ben. Picture does not communicate these different meanings.
findings.repair: Vary to checklist/contact inspection, uncertain reaction, empty inbox, settled output and relieved head/body.

findings.observation: Large run of same desk/stack composition; repeated body/head pose with headline changes provides little visual escalation across more departments, queues and obligations.
findings.repair: Differentiate incoming sources, increasing queues, department requests and action/consequence shots.

findings.observation: Final project has 218 shots but shot-ledger has 217 pre-opening-replacement sentence entries, so actual shot numbering diverges after opening insertion.
findings.repair: Rebuild ledger from final project shot timeline with associated original sentence IDs.

retracted_suspicions.status: Unconfirmed/retracted; likely neighboring cell text, not an actual per-frame overlap.

positive_observations: Near-white faint-grid background and limited accent colors retained.
Characters are slender and heads/limbs generally coherent in the inspected stills.
One-line captions appear within the bottom band and are generally legible in inspected sheets/full-size frames.
Original story conflict and ending are clear in source text.
limits: No actual continuous encoded film playback reviewed.
No soundtrack listening or voice intelligibility comparison performed.
Stills cannot establish motion, contact through action, pacing, caption synchronization, SFX timing or audio quality.
No sample-equivalence or full-film acceptance asserted.
Any parent repairs made after this snapshot require fresh inspection.
